messages:
alex: CI turned red on my PR (#4289) at job `serve-integration-1082`, failing `prefetch_latency_assertion_test`. failure is intermittent, saw it twice in a row in the same job run. log: https://ci.redwood.local/job/1082/console

alex: failure snippet:
```
E       AssertionError: expected prefetch queue length > 0, got 0
serve/runtime/prefetch_manager_test.py:67: AssertionError
```

alex: I can't repro locally (ran the test 50x) but CI hits it. can someone kick a rerun or help bisect? cc @tasha @mike

tasha: on it, rerunning job now. will also check artifacts.

ci-bot: Re-run requested by tasha for job `serve-integration-1082`. New attempt queued: https://ci.redwood.local/job/1082/attempt/2

mike: thanks. fwiw we saw a similar symptom earlier with `prefetch` where timing + the new executor jitter created empty queue windows. increasing small timeout helped. not identical but maybe related.

jen: alex, can you paste the exact pytest invocation you used locally? want to match seeds/timeouts.

alex: `pytest -k prefetch_latency_assertion_test -q --maxfail=1 -x` and I looped it with `for i in {1..50}; do pytest -k prefetch_latency_assertion_test -q || break; done`

priya: I'm looking at the CI artifact bundle now. found the failing trace and the test used `time.sleep(0.01)` in a few places. suspect flakiness from relying on real sleeps.

tasha: rerun attempt 2 finished: PASS. but attempt 1 and the original failed, so flaky for sure. job artifacts for attempt 1/3 attached at https://ci.redwood.local/job/1082/attempt/1/artifacts.zip

mike: can we add a deterministic scheduler for the unit test or replace `time.sleep` with a mocked clock? that usually stabilizes these timing races.

alex: happy to open a quick PR to mock the clock if we agree. patch could be small: replace `time.sleep` with `fake_clock.advance()` in the test and inject a test-only scheduler.

jen: before changing test, can we try a targeted bisect on recent runtime changes? if the flake frequency increased after commit range `main~15..main~5` that narrows it. alex, do you know which changes touched prefetch manager recently?

alex: last 2 weeks we landed the executor jitter patch (PR 4211) and a prefetch refactor (PR 4256). both are candidates.

priya: I'll run a quick git-bisect locally across those two PRs tomorrow morning and report back.

tasha: note: we should avoid reintroducing slow sleeps just to pass CI. mock clock preferred. if bisect doesn't point to a single PR, let's add a flaky skip marker and follow up with a fix.

mike: +1 for mock clock. also add a short comment with `// flaky: tracked in #4289` so it's searchable.

ci-bot: Rerun attempt 3 for job `serve-integration-1082` completed: FAIL (same assertion).

alex: ugh. attempt 2 was a fluke then. thanks for bisecting, priya — that should help. I'll start a draft PR to move the test to a fake clock harness and ping review.

jen: awesome. if you can, attach a small repro harness (single test script) that reliably reproduces when run under `pytest -k prefetch_latency_assertion_test` with real clock, that'll speed review.

alex: will do. tagging this thread with the action items:
- alex: open draft PR to use fake clock and add repro harness
- priya: run git-bisect across PRs 4211/4256 tomorrow
- tasha: add a temporary flaky marker on the CI job if bisect doesn't find culprit by EOD

mike: thanks team. keep updates here and ping #eng-runtime if you need infra help. :thumbsup:
